_what_this_record_is: A DISCOVERY record, not a single-study record. It holds a ranked shortlist of candidate reproducibility anchors for GraphFLA metrics, one `paper` block per candidate under `candidates`, and `overlaps` entries keyed by `paper_key`. Where the target was cheap and the input already local, the reproduction was attempted and the true outcome recorded; everything else is `not_attempted` or `input_unavailable` with a reason.

overlaps.graphfla_call: analysis.fitness_distribution(ls) on the max-normalised bundled fitness
overlaps.reason: The bundled Tu2022_T7.csv is platykurtic (Fisher kurtosis -0.38) over the range -1.1766..0.8512, the shape of a log-transformed quantity, whereas Li's printed 46.51 / 0.0000 is the shape of a raw enrichment measure concentrated at zero with heavy tails. Undoing a base-10 log moves GraphFLA to 0.0289 / 39.39, much closer but still not matching. Tu2022_T7.csv and Tu2022_TEV.csv share an identical minimum of -1.1766, the signature of a curation-time floor, yet TEV reproduces exactly on the bundled scale while T7 does not. This is a DATA-PROVENANCE question about a bundled file, in the same class as the documented tenfold Weinreich2006 error, NOT a metric defect.

overlaps.locator: Table S1, column 'Fraction of non-magnitude epistasis'
overlaps.quote: For each active variant, we assigned an epistasis type for each possible double substitution at chosen sites. We then calculated the fraction of epistasis type for each starting variant in the landscape. To enhance relevance to DE navigability, we incorporated additive interactions into magnitude epistasis, and merged sign and reciprocal sign epistasis into non-magnitude epistasis. Missing values are omitted.
overlaps.definition_quote: For landscapes containing fitness data for variants with stop codons, "active" variants were defined as those 1.96 standard deviations above the mean fitness of all sequences containing stop codons, which are expected to be inactive. For GB1, T7, and TEV we followed the cutoffs set by the authors, based on the detection limit of their fitness measurement system.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Three divergences: (1) Li et al. restrict starting variants to ACTIVE ones, GraphFLA censuses all squares; (2) Li et al. fold ADDITIVE squares into magnitude, GraphFLA's three-way motif classification does not have an additive class; (3) Li et al. average per-starting-variant fractions, GraphFLA pools over all squares. The active cutoff cannot be rebuilt from the bundled CSVs because stop-codon rows are not present.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, Kuo et al. 2020 column, row 'r/s', parenthesised (average-fitness) value
overlaps.definition_quote: The roughness value r is the square root of the mean squared fitness residual from the above regression and s is the average of the absolute values of the linear coefficients β i (i =1, 2, …, and n).
overlaps.definition_divergence: The formula is identical to GraphFLA's, but the ALLELE CODING differs and s is not invariant to it. The authors' notebooks build the design with BASES=['A','T','C','G'] over RNA sequences spelling U, so no U column is ever created and U becomes the implicit reference level; GraphFLA uses pd.get_dummies(drop_first=True), which drops the alphabetically first level, A. Same column space, so r is identical; different s, so the ratio differs by 8.9%.
overlaps.reason: Under the paper's own reference-allele coding GraphFLA's formula gives 4.0628980 against a printed 4.063 - an exact match at the printed precision, and Ridge(alpha=1) as the notebook actually calls gives 4.0630308, also 4.063, so the penalty is immaterial. GraphFLA's DEFAULT coding gives 3.7324439. FINDING: r_s_ratio is not invariant to the choice of reference allele on multi-allelic landscapes, and the current choice is undocumented and arbitrary.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, Domingo et al. 2018 column, row 'r/s', parenthesised value
overlaps.definition_quote: When a landscape has four instead of two states per variable site, we adjusted the above additive model to F(x) = β0 + Σ βiA xiA + βiT xiT + βiC xiC + βiG xiG, ... and s = Σ (|βiA| + |βiT| + |βiC| + |βiG|) / 3n
overlaps.definition_divergence: The Methods give formulas only for 2-state and 4-state sites; Domingo has 6 biallelic and 4 triallelic sites. Under the authors' actual coding the design has 17 columns, and at the three sites with no U (pos1 {A,G}, pos5 {A,C}, pos8 {A,G}) every observed allele keeps a column, so the design is rank-deficient and the individual beta are not identifiable. Their Domingo r/s is therefore both convention- and solver-dependent.

input.preprocessing: none; fitness column used as-is (already log-transformed Wrightian fitness, WT = 0)

overlaps.reason: 2.0566631 under the paper's coding against a printed 2.102, a 2.2% gap. Not closed by any coding or transform tested (drop-first, drop-U, min-norm full one-hot; denominators n, ncoef, 3n, 4n; raw/ln/log2/log10/min-max fitness; observed-only and 0-filled complete product space; OLS and Ridge at alpha in {0.01,0.1,1,10}). The residual cause is an input difference: the authors recompute fitness from raw read counts with their own generation-ratio formula (get_fitness in trna_Domingo/Generate_raw_data.ipynb) rather than using the published fitness column. Bundled file is at full precision (4,176 distinct values), so rounding is not the cause.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, Kuo et al. 2020 column, row 'N max', parenthesised value
overlaps.definition_quote: A genotype is considered a local fitness maximum if it is fitter than all of its neighboring genotypes, which differ from the focal genotype by one point mutation.
overlaps.definition_divergence: GraphFLA matches the authors' CODE, not their prose. Their notebook is `if np.sum(fit <= y[neighbor_list[i]]) == 0` with neighbour lists built over OBSERVED sequences only - strictly fitter than every present neighbour, absent neighbours ignored. The Methods instead claim missing neighbours were 'treated ... as having a fitness of 0', which the code does not do.
overlaps.reason: -0.58%. An independent numpy recount under the strict rule gives 2388; GraphFLA's 2390 is 2388 strict peaks plus 2 two-genotype plateaus with no fitter neighbour; counting ties as peaks gives 2425. The printed 2404 lies in that band but matches none of them. Cause: the bundled Kuo2020.csv is rounded to 3 decimal places (only 2,473 distinct fitness values across 197,890 rows), which manufactures ties and makes any tie-sensitive statistic precision-limited at the 0.5-1% level. The authors recomputed fitness from read counts at full precision. ALSO FOUND: sum(graph.vs['is_lo']) = 2392 while n_lo = 2390 - n_lo counts plateaus, is_lo flags their members, and the two accessors disagree with no documentation.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, Domingo et al. 2018 column, row 'N max', parenthesised value
overlaps.definition_quote: A genotype is considered a local fitness maximum if it is fitter than all of its neighboring genotypes, which differ from the focal genotype by one point mutation.
overlaps.definition_divergence: As above: GraphFLA matches the code (strict, observed neighbours only), not the prose.
overlaps.reason: +23%. An independent strict recount also gives 86, so GraphFLA is self-consistent. Imputing 0 for missing neighbours as the prose describes gives 42, which is further from 70, not closer; the 4-state site model gives 86 (absent) or 34 (imputed 0). The printed 70 is reachable from none of them, so the authors' Domingo fitness values differ from the bundled column despite an identical genotype count.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, row 'F rse', parenthesised values
overlaps.quote: For each genotype pair, reciprocal sign epistasis is recorded if both genotypes are either fitter or less fit than the two intermediate genotypes between them. F rse is the proportion of genotype pairs that exhibit reciprocal sign epistasis.
overlaps.definition_quote: For the three empirical landscapes, we examined all genotype pairs from genotypes with estimated fitness for F rse estimation.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Substantively the same quantity as GraphFLA's reciprocal_sign fraction - the notebook's cal_epi counts both orientations, matching GraphFLA. Two caveats: (1) their square enumeration keeps a square only when BOTH intermediate indices exceed the starting genotype's index, silently dropping squares whose intermediate sorts earlier in file order - a row-order artefact in both numerator and denominator; (2) utils.py's cal_epi, used for the simulated landscapes, counts only one orientation, so the authors' two implementations disagree with each other.
overlaps.reason: Kuo +0.65%, Domingo +4.1%. The Kuo agreement to within 0.65% on a 197,890-genotype landscape is strong evidence the two statistics are the same quantity; the residual is attributable to their index-order filter plus the 3-dp rounding of the bundled Kuo file. This is the closest thing found to a second classify_epistasis anchor, and it would become one on the authors' full-precision inputs.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, row '1-γ', parenthesised values
overlaps.quote: γ describes the correlation between the fitness effect of a mutation in one genetic background and that in another background differing from the first background at one site. We calculated γ by following a previous study (Ferretti et al., 2016) and regarded 1-γ as the ruggedness measure in our analysis so that it increases with ruggedness.
overlaps.definition_quote: cal_gamma (empirical notebooks): cov = Σ (y1-y0)(y3-y2) + Σ (y2-y0)(y3-y1); cov = cov/(2*n_squares); var = np.var([y[nb] - y[i] for every i, every neighbour nb]); return cov/var
overlaps.definition_divergence: Despite citing Ferretti et al. 2016, neither of the authors' two implementations is Ferretti eq. (3). utils.py computes a CENTRED covariance over a ddof=0 variance, i.e. a regression slope. The empirical notebooks compute a non-centred second moment over the squares divided by the variance of ALL single-step fitness differences in the whole graph. GraphFLA's denominator is 0.5*(Σb² + ΣB²) over the SAME square-derived effects. Different denominator populations, hence different statistics.
overlaps.reason: Kuo -21%, Domingo +2.2%. The landscape-dependent sign and size of the gap is exactly what a denominator swap produces, and is incompatible with a constant rescaling. DO NOT tune gamma toward Table 1. Ferretti et al. 2016 remains the only gamma anchor; Song & Zhang is ruled out as a second one on definitional grounds.

overlaps.locator: Table 1, row 'E', parenthesised values
overlaps.quote: Therefore, E equals 1 − E 1 ∑ j = 1 n E j , where E j is the epistasis of the j th order.
overlaps.definition_quote: Given that genotypes with zero reads were discarded in the original paper, we filled all missing genotypes with fitness of 0 to obtain a complete fitness landscape to calculate E.
overlaps.definition_divergence: Theirs is a Walsh-Hadamard variance share, (ΣE² - E0² - ΣE1²)/(ΣE² - E0²), computed on a COMPLETED 2^10 biallelic sub-landscape. GraphFLA's is an unregularised one-hot polynomial OLS R-squared on the observed subset. Different estimand and different support. A third paper/code inconsistency: the Methods say missing cells were filled with 0, but the notebook interpolates them with Ridge.
overlaps.reason: Kuo -12%, Domingo +28%. Same verdict as Papkou Fig. S21 already in LEDGER.md: a penalised/orthogonal-basis variance share is not an unregularised OLS R-squared. Measured to size the divergence, not offered as a target.

overlaps.locator: arXiv:1507.00041 section 2.5 eq. (15), restated in the Discussion
overlaps.quote: γ ∗ is directly related to the number of square motifs with sign and reciprocal sign epistasis as γ ∗ = 1 − φs − 2φrs.
overlaps.definition_quote: The measure γ ∗ is defined as before: γ ∗ = Cor[s∗(g), s∗(g1)]
overlaps.definition_divergence: None. This is the defining paper, and the identity must hold between GraphFLA's gamma_star and its own classify_epistasis fractions on any landscape, with no external data required.

input.path: data/BioSequence/{Weinreich2006Tan2011_Weinreich2006, deVisser2009, Mira2015_TEM_AM, Lozovsky2009Jiang2013_Lozovsky2009, Domingo2018, Lite2020_ParD2, Johnston2024_TrpB3A}.csv

overlaps.reason: DEFECT LOCALISED. The identity holds to float round-off on five landscapes and to 4e-6 on one incomplete landscape, but fails by 0.0449 on the 32-genotype TEM landscape. Independent enumeration: that landscape has 80 square motifs of which 39 contain at least one tied (zero-magnitude) fitness effect, leaving 41 classifiable; an independent census of those 41 gives magnitude 29, sign 10, reciprocal-sign 2, exactly GraphFLA's reported 0.707317/0.243902/0.048780, so classify_epistasis is internally correct on the squares it counts but its denominator excludes every tied square. gamma_star separately drops zero-sign effects via np.sign, over a different population (edge pairs, not squares). Three mutually inconsistent answers result: gamma_star 0.613636, eq. (15) over the 41 classifiable squares 0.658537, eq. (15) over all 80 squares 0.825. CONCLUSION: gamma_star and classify_epistasis use different conventions for zero-magnitude fitness effects, breaking Ferretti eq. (15) on any landscape with exact fitness ties. Affects the whole MIC/doubling-dilution class including the 15 Mira2015_TEM_* files; Mira2015_TEM_AM happens to pass, so a single smoke test will not catch it.

verdict_reason: Seven ranked candidates, of which three were actually reproduced against because their inputs were already local. The pass moved two metric families. (1) fitness_distribution went from NO anchor to a 14-landscape exact anchor: Li et al. 2025 Cell Systems Table S1 prints the fitted-Cauchy location and the kurtosis for 16 combinatorially complete protein landscapes, GraphFLA reproduces BOTH at the printed precision on 14 of the 15 bundled locally, and the paper's Methods name the exact scipy calls GraphFLA uses - it is almost certainly the implementation's source. (2) r_s_ratio gained a second anchor: Song & Zhang 2021 Table 1 r/s = 4.063 on Kuo 2020, reproduced as 4.0628980, but only under the paper's reference-allele coding - which exposed that GraphFLA's r_s_ratio is not invariant to which one-hot level is dropped (3.732 vs 4.063 on the same data). gamma gained a second printed value (Ferretti et al. 2018 Heredity / arXiv:1507.00041: TEM gamma = 0.85, gamma* = 0.59, r/s = 0.43, peaks 1, sinks 1), of which only the peak count reproduces; the hypothesis that the documented tenfold defect in the bundled Weinreich CSV explained that mismatch was tested and REJECTED. Song & Zhang was ruled out as a gamma anchor on definitional grounds after reading the authors' own code. Separately, Ferretti's eq. (15) gamma* = 1 - phi_s - 2*phi_rs gave a free internal consistency test that GraphFLA satisfies to 1e-16 on five tie-free landscapes and VIOLATES by 0.0449 on the 32-genotype TEM landscape, localising a real tie-handling inconsistency between gamma_star and classify_epistasis that affects the whole MIC/doubling-dilution class. Best unworked target left: Weinreich et al. 2018 J Stat Phys Table 3, three printed Fourier-Walsh order-wise variance profiles with all three inputs already local. Ruled out and recorded so no later session repeats them: Schenk 2013 MBE, Fragata 2018 Heredity and Schulz 2025 PNAS (all plot-only); de Visser & Krug 2014 and Bank 2022 (no tables at all); arXiv 1303.3842 (never peer-reviewed, mutation records not fitnesses); the MAGELLAN preprint (never published, prints no gamma value); Blanquart & Bataillon 2016 (different statistics); Weinreich 2013 COGD (plotted, two small exact unit tests survive); Hinz 2024 and Ghenu 2023 (gamma plot-only, reference implementations downloadable). gamma_star has a printed number but no second one; fdc has its origin identified but is blocked on three pre-DOI function definitions; four of the seven fitness_distribution descriptors have no published origin at all, which is a settled negative rather than an open question.
graphfla_observations_not_acted_on: gamma_star and classify_epistasis use different conventions for zero-magnitude fitness effects, breaking Ferretti et al. eq. (15) on any landscape with exact fitness ties. Minimal reproducer: data/BioSequence/Weinreich2006Tan2011_Weinreich2006.csv, 32 rows, 39 of its 80 squares tied. Mira2015_TEM_AM passes, so a single smoke test will not catch it.

r_s_ratio is not invariant to the choice of reference allele on multi-allelic landscapes: 3.7324439 (drop first category, GraphFLA's default) vs 4.0628980 (drop U, the published convention) on data/BioSequence/Kuo2020.csv. The convention is undocumented.

sum(graph.vs['is_lo']) != landscape.n_lo when plateaus are present: 2392 vs 2390 on data/BioSequence/Kuo2020.csv. n_lo counts plateaus, is_lo flags their members; both defensible, the silent disagreement is not.

fitness_distribution's docstring claims the whole descriptor set is unitless and scale-invariant. cauchy_loc is a location parameter in fitness units and is neither scale- nor shift-invariant - which is exactly why Li et al. max-normalise before reporting it.

data/BioSequence/Tu2022_T7.csv is on a fitness scale inconsistent with its sibling Tu2022_TEV.csv relative to Li et al.'s inputs, and does not invert cleanly under exp, 2**f or 10**f. Both files share an identical minimum of -1.1766, the signature of a curation-time floor. A data-provenance question in the same class as the documented tenfold Weinreich2006 error.

data/BioSequence/Kuo2020.csv is rounded to 3 decimal places: 2,473 distinct fitness values across 197,890 rows. Any tie-sensitive statistic on this file is precision-limited at roughly the 0.5-1% level.
